title: Office visits: bladder, sleep, drink and tremor

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 8, 12, 17 and 23. Each question cites its item. Provisional grouping; review before trusting.

questions.q: Uncomplicated urinary leakage in a 60-year-old. Which belong in the initial evaluation?
questions.why: History decides whether it is transient or chronic and which subtype. The three imaging and instrumented tests wait for complicated or refractory cases.

questions.q: Which finding at the first visit for incontinence calls for specialist referral?
questions.why: Fistula is the other red flag. The three distractors are risk factors, and the first-line treatments are weight loss, pelvic floor training and fluid advice.

questions.q: Which is a component of sleep hygiene education within CBT for insomnia?
questions.a: Waking at the same time every day
questions.why: Cutting time in bed belongs to sleep restriction, a separate part of CBT-I. Stimulus control is the third part: bed only when sleepy, bedroom for sleep and sex.

questions.q: In sleep restriction, time in bed is extended once sleep efficiency reaches what level?
questions.why: Then by 15 minutes a week. Sleep efficiency is time asleep over time in bed.

questions.q: Four weeks of poor sleep after a bereavement. What is the first step in management?
d: A two-week course of a hypnotic
questions.why: Acute insomnia runs at least 3 nights a week for 1 week to 3 months and usually has a cause. CBT-I is first-line when the patient wants to avoid drugs.

questions.q: Two weeks sober and asking for a drug to stay that way. Which is recommended?
questions.why: Fewer than 2% of people with alcohol use disorder are prescribed anything. Acamprosate carries the strongest rating for maintaining abstinence already achieved.

questions.q: What is gabapentin's role in alcohol use disorder?
questions.a: Preventing withdrawal, even while still drinking
d: Maintaining abstinence once it is achieved
questions.why: Topiramate is the one that reduces heavy drinking in someone not yet abstinent. Acamprosate belongs to the abstinent.

questions.q: What does the evidence say about disulfiram for alcohol use disorder?
d: SOR B for reducing heavy drinking
questions.why: It still has its users, but on the evidence it is the one of the four the guideline cannot endorse.

questions.q: Shuffling gait, resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity at 75. Which are first-line drugs?
questions.why: Rasagiline is an MAO-B inhibitor and pramipexole a non-ergot dopamine agonist, the other two first-line classes. Amitriptyline and fluoxetine are on the Beers list, and the flat affect here is parkinsonism, not depression.

questions.q: Which feature separates the tremor of Parkinson disease from essential tremor?
d: It is symmetric from the start
questions.why: Essential tremor is an action tremor, often symmetric, often eased by alcohol, and propranolol treats it. The resting pill-rolling tremor gets dopamine replacement.
